Command: Do not leave any of the Passover lamb until morning
Summary: No part of the Passover lamb may remain uneaten until morning; what is left must be burned with fire.
Commandment: Leave none of the Passover lamb until the morning; whatever remains until morning, burn with fire.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The New Testament reads the Passover lamb as fulfilled in Christ, our Passover sacrificed for us (1 Corinthians 5:7). The ritual meal form belongs to Israel's covenant calendar, not to Christian observance.
Purpose: Scripture's stated context: the meal is eaten in haste on the night of deliverance from Egypt, ready to depart (Exodus 12:11).
Function: Nothing of the lamb was to survive the night, and that urgency is the mark of a ceremonial law: a rite bound to one night. Its goal was to keep the Passover meal inside the night of deliverance — eaten in haste, ready to depart, with nothing carried over into ordinary days. It addressed no particular evil — its work was remembrance, not restraint. What remained was burned, so the meal could not drift into an ordinary leftover.
